chapter: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
title: Touring the northwest for Pops McElroy
summary: During the war Goosby is in the Portland shipyards; Fields tours there under Pops McElroy's ballroom bookings.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So anyway, as I said we played there several times, but then years passed and went on and we didn't hear anything about Enid because I just happened not to be in that area, but during World War II, a lot of the okies migrated to the coast, and Dewey happened to go into the shipyard of Portland.

Yeah, Portland, Oregon, and of course I didn't know anything, I forgot about Dewey, and I was touring the west coast, the northwest, and Pops McElroy, who brought names in, he'd have Lunceford, Duke and all, but anyway, an area booker I got connected with, and they set a tour for me through there.
I played it with Count Basie, Lucky Millinder.
Yeah, he used to play all the big ones. Pops McElroy.
His son later took it over, after Pop.
Well, Pops was living then and so that was in the early forties, and so we went on this tour, and as I said, I hadn't thought about Dewey, any connection and I was booked for a

black dance, an all colored dance, on a Thursday night, and I went on down--if you've ever been in that area, Seaside, Oregon, and we went on down to Seaside, Oregon Friday night and then we were back to Portland that Saturday for an all white dance.
